ranking.rationale: Educational attainment is one of the strongest and most stable predictors of income across states, capturing durable human-capital differences with less geographic brittleness than occupation or birthplace.
Usual hours worked per week is a strong, broadly stable predictor of income across states and complements SCHL by capturing labor supply intensity rather than geography or state-specific artifacts.
Age is a strong, broadly stable predictor of income across states and complements education and hours worked without relying on geography or brittle local artifacts.

Occupation is one of the strongest remaining predictors of income and tends to generalize better across states than geography-linked or demographic proxy features; it adds substantial stable signal beyond education, hours worked, and age.

Class of worker adds stable labor-market information about earnings potential and complements education, occupation, age, and hours worked without relying as heavily on geography or brittle state-specific artifacts.

Marital status is a relatively stable socioeconomic signal that can add predictive value beyond age, education, hours worked, occupation, and class of worker, while being less geography-specific and less brittle than birthplace or race.
Household relationship can add stable context about family/household role that may correlate with income across states without being as geography-specific as birthplace or race.
Sex can add modest stable signal for income through labor-market patterns and hours/occupation interactions, while being less geography-specific than birthplace or race.

Race can add some stable signal through persistent labor-market and education disparities, while birthplace is more geography- and migration-pattern-specific and more likely to encode brittle state-level artifacts.

Place of birth can add some signal about migration-linked labor and education patterns, but it is also a strong geography/demographic shortcut and likely less stable across states than the already selected core socioeconomic features.
